obligation: Acquirer notice of suspected card data compromise (contractual)
citation: Merchant agreement with the acquiring bank (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Requirement 12.10.1 (N81-R03)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data: card numbers exposed from ticket notes or paper, or a tampered payment terminal
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspecting a compromise (merchant agreement term). Clock starts at suspicion, not confirmation

obligation: Card brand compromise procedures, including forensic investigation (contractual)
citation: Payment brand operating rules, applied through the acquirer - not law
trigger: Acquirer or card brand opens a compromise case
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified); may require a PCI Forensic Investigator
notify: Acquirer; card brands through the acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the acquirer opens a case; brand rules were not verified

obligation: Manufacturer A notice of suspected customer data incident (contractual)
citation: Manufacturer A authorized service provider agreement (fictional term)
trigger: Suspected incident involving customer data or devices handled under the program (for example a technician copying device content, or exposure of warranty customers' records)
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (program agreement term)

trigger: Incident affecting a business account's devices or data
applies_at_this_tier: Yes for the affected accounts - contractual

trigger: Unauthorized access of data in electronic form containing personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a name with medical, biometric, or geolocation information, a name with a financial account or card number plus required code, and an email address or user name with a password (501.171(1)(g)). Good-faith employee access for a business purpose is not a breach (501.171(1)(a)); snooping or copying is not good faith
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Notice by mail or email ((4)(d)) with the content in (4)(e)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for exported passcode and password notes; counsel decides for device content

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines in writing that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested (for example a police investigation of a technician)

trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Document in writing, keep for at least 5 years, and provide to the Department of Legal Affairs within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Possible for a contained device incident with no copies; counsel decides

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (15 more days if good cause is given in writing within 30 days). Content listed in (3)(b)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500+ Florida residents (likely for a SYS-01 export)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (15 U.S.C. 1681a(p))

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A third-party agent (for example the SYS-01 vendor, cloud provider, or chatbot vendor) has a breach of a system it maintains for the company
deadline: No later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred; the agent must give the company the information it needs to notify

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N81-R02)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents of other states (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example without unreasonable delay or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 9% of tickets are mail-in customers from other states; counsel applies each state's law

trigger: Suspected theft of customer data or devices by a workforce member, or a criminal compromise of card data or accounts
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0-2); coordinate with counsel before contacting police about an employee
notify: Local police (insider theft); FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office (card data or account compromise)

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors)

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

trigger: Notification event at a financial institution involving 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company extends no credit and is not a financial institution under Part 314 (P03 G-142)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope: critical infrastructure entities above the SBA size standard, or meeting a sector criterion regardless of size; the company is below its SBA size standard

trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
